text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Monday.

GERMANY - Bund futures posted one of their biggest declines in weeks as uncertainty about European monetary union and technical factors sparked heavy selling. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.39, down 1.04 from Friday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended more than three-quarters of a point weaker after the election date was set for May 1, as widely anticipated, but the sell-off in Bunds was a more important market factor. The June gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-12/32, down 25/32 from Friday's settlement price.

FRANCE - Bond futures came under pressure amid widespread selling in European bond markets sparked by uncertainty about European monetary union and nervousness about the chance of a U.S. rate rise next week. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.32, down 0.98 from Friday's settlement price.

ITALY - Bond futures slumped by late afternoon well over a full point as investors worried about possible delays to Europe's single currency with most other European bond markets tumbling as well. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 124.28, down 1.38 from Friday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened lower with the market unable to shake off its fears that the Federal Reserve will soon raise interest rates. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-14/32, down 13/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.98 percent.

JAPAN - The key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract closed easier on profit-taking after hitting a record high of 126.88. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 126.46, down 0.09 from Friday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market had a low key start to the week in terms of actual issuance. Argentina announced international borrowing plans for Q2. KEXIM was expected to launch a $500 million 10-year global bond later this week. PUMA, Australia's largest private sector mortgage-backed bond issuer, was due with a $700 million three-tranche FRN. Borrowers considering sterling will likely hold back, where possible, until after an expected May 1 election. Bank of Nova Scotia set a $200 million two-year deal.
